metadata.scenario_context: Emily is preparing to move into a new home and is planning to host a housewarming party. One of her neighbors who are homosexuals. Mike and Kim will attend Emily’s housewarming party.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China would like to have homosexuals as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Nigeria would not like to have homosexuals as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to Emily’s housewarming party
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have homosexuals as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily’s housewarming party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have homosexuals as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Hey Kim, have you thought about what we should bring to Emily's housewarming party? I was thinking... maybe some chrysanthemums? They’re beautiful and symbolize good luck. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Chrysanthemums? Hmm... They are nice, but I think we should consider something more *practical*. Maybe a nice set of kitchen utensils or something for her new place? It feels more... useful for a housewarming.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I don’t really see meaningful differences here. I mean, at the end of the day, it’s all the same. People figure it out, you know? Whether we bring flowers or utensils, it’s about celebrating Emily. I think chrysanthemums would be nice, and with experience you can handle any situation. Besides, I think having different types of neighbors can be good... like having diverse perspectives. But anyway, what do you think about chrysanthemums?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Kim
